info.name: Grip Security Public API (v1.0)
info.description:
Reference for the Grip Security public API used by the FairTPRM Shadow SaaS
integration. Regenerated from a Grip tenant's live specification
(`https://<tenant>.dep.grip.security/public/openapi.json`); every tenant also
serves interactive Swagger UI at `https://<tenant>.dep.grip.security/public/docs`.
Official documentation portal: https://apidocs.grip.security/docs/api-docs/16b5e21308a0e-grip

Authentication: send the tenant administrator API key in the `access-token`
HTTP header on every request (security scheme `APIKeyHeader`). Bearer,
X-API-Key and Basic are rejected with 401.

Pagination: list endpoints accept `offset` (zero-based) and `limit` (max 200
for most lists) and also return a `next` response header. Grip can return a
short page (for example 199 of 200) in the middle of a list, so advance
`offset` by the requested page size and stop only on an empty page; a short
page is not the end of the list.

Set the collection variables `baseUrl` (your tenant's /public base) and `accessToken` (tenant admin API key) before sending. The accessToken is sent as the `access-token` header on every request.

Please note: this endpoint will be deprecated as of September 21, 2025.

Retrieve the status of an offboarding workflow, with results for supported applications. 

This endpoint is intended for automation. 

It doesn't reflect the status of the workflow the same way the Grip portal would. 

With this endpoint, any access revocation tasks that are still under manual review will be reported as finished. 

This is unlike the Grip portal where workflows are considered in progress while being reviewed.

This endpoint will only work on offboarding workflows executed on a single employee.

Run a workflow for the workflow ID.
Every workflow should contain at least one of the following:
    
* app_name / app_id in case of Application-based workflow
    
* identity_email / identity_id in case of Identity-based workflow

Trigger a password reset run for a CyberArk-managed carrier. Provide `carrier` to select the carrier and `tickets` to scope the run to specific accounts by office/location, each with an optional ticket id. Omit `tickets` to reset all accounts of the carrier. All CyberArk tiles sharing a matched username are reset once and updated together.

Discover ITDR remediation actions, the SaaS apps and connected tenants they apply to, and the target fields required to trigger each one.

Trigger an ITDR remediation action on a connected SaaS integration without an ITDR alert. Every call writes a Grip activity log entry. For GitHub, username-wide revocation is supported for classic PATs, fine-grained PATs, OAuth app tokens, and SSH keys. Exact revocation is supported for classic PATs, OAuth app tokens, GitHub App tokens, and SSH keys. Exact fine-grained PAT revocation requires GitHub App authentication and is not supported by the connected integration. Supply identityId or a resolvable email on GitHub credential actions to populate Related Identity in the activity log.
